rule: Call through a parameter, local variable or stored property holding a function (callback, closure, fn pointer, delegate) → callee is the variable's name, `call_type` callback, confidence unknown. | Code outside a method body: the caller is its location. Field/val initializer → `Type#field`; C# property accessor → `Type#Prop` (get) / `Type#Prop=` (set); Ruby setter → `Type#x=`; `static {}` block → `Type#<clinit>`. Non-lazy initializers also get an `implicit` edge from `<clinit>`/`<init>`; lazy ones do not.
source: KNOWN_GAP: delegate fields and => getters are under-resolved
notes: Expression-bodied properties `public int Result => …` are get accessors: caller App.Calc#Result / App.Calc#Scaled (SPEC: C# property accessor → Type#Prop). An expression-bodied method (`Twice(int v) => …`) has the method as caller. op (a field of the scanned delegate type Op) and transform (a Func field) are stored properties holding a function: calling them, bare or through this., is callback, unknown, callee = the field name. The delegate type declaration and the constructor's assignments are not calls.
